title: USC star JuJu Watkins could change Toronto Tempo's future, providing she declares for WNBA draft
summary: Most WNBA executives have long considered JuJu Watkins a generational prospect, a player potentially on par with A’Ja Wilson, Cailtin Clark or Paige Bueckers as far as altering a franchise's future.

image.caption: USC star JuJu Watkins is the consensus No. 1 pick for next year's WNBA draft, though she has yet to declare herself eligible. (Ethan Miller/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Basketball·Analysis
Most WNBA executives have long considered JuJu Watkins a generational prospect, a player potentially on par with A’Ja Wilson, Cailtin Clark or Paige Bueckers as far as altering a franchise's future.
A generational prospect, 21-year-old wants to win NCAA title before turning pro
· for CBC Sports
· Posted: Nov 16, 2026 8:32 AM EST | Last Updated: 26 minutes ago

If you want a glimpse into the future of the WNBA, we encourage you to watch highlights from Sunday’s women’s college basketball game between the University of South Carolina and the University of Southern California. The game was marketed as “The Real SC” (both teams use “SC” as part of their athletic identity) but calling it The WNBA Draft Invitational would have been more accurate.

There were future first-round picks all across Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, S.C., including a six-pack of prospects from No. 1-ranked South Carolina (Joyce Edwards, Chloe Kitts, Tessa Johnson, Agot Makeer, Jerzy Robinson and Ashlyn Watkins). The No. 3-ranked USC star contingent included sophomore guards Jazzy Davidson, Kennedy Smith and freshman forward-guard Saniyah Hall, the top-ranked high school recruit entering the season. All of the players above are projected as first-round picks between the 2027 and 2029 WNBA drafts.

But in a game featuring future WNBA stars, there was one prospect who stood above the rest as far as name recognition and possibility — USC guard-forward JuJu Watkins, a six-foot-two senior wing with the ability to score from three levels (at the rim, mid-range and three-point distance). Most WNBA executives have long considered Watkins a generational prospect, a player potentially on par with A’Ja Wilson, Cailtin Clark or Paige Bueckers as far as altering a franchise's future.

On Sunday, the 21-year-old Watkins showed flashes of what she can be. She has one of the most artistically pleasing pull-up jumpers in the history of women’s college basketball and unlike many prolific scorers, she attacks defences with the intensity of a starving pit bull. You win titles in the WNBA with elite front-court players and Watkins can swing seamlessly between the forward and guard spots, making her a difficult challenge for defences. Her potential is vast — she missed the entire 2025–26 season due to a torn right ACL and looks like she has not missed a beat. But the complete product is still a couple of years away. Watkins finished with 25 points on 8 of 20 shooting against South Carolina but also had five turnovers. (South Carolina’s big-game experience and deeper frontcourt talent was the difference; they held on for an 89-85 win.)

Like most WNBA executives, Toronto Tempo general manager Monica Wright Rogers watched Sunday afternoon’s game very closely. But Wright Rogers had far more stake than most. The Tempo entered Sunday night’s WNBA lottery with a 32.9 per cent chance at the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft, tied with the Houston Comets (formerly the Connecticut Sun) for the best odds .
By now you likely know what happened: Toronto landed the No. 1 pick.

items: Toronto Tempo earn No. 1 pick after winning 2027 WNBA draft lottery

blocks.text: ANEESAH CALLED IT 🇨🇦 Morrow had a feeling tonight would be special, and @TempoBasketball is walking away with the No. 1 overall pick! WNBA Draft Lottery 2027 | @StateStreetETFs SPY https://t.co/bPtvhbcgF5—WNBA

“There were no words for the emotion that filled our conference room where I was with the strategy team and our comms [communication] team,” Rogers said when asked what it was like when she saw the news on television. “Our hearts were beating out of our chest.”

One of the unique twists to the WNBA draft puzzle this year is that the top draft-eligible players in women’s college basketball can all return for another year in college because of the NCAA's new "5-in-5" eligibility rule which allows Division I and II women's basketball players up to five years of eligibility to compete in five seasons. Thus, Watkins has the option for a fifth year at USC as a medical redshirt given she missed last season with an ACL injury. Texas forward Madison Booker, Notre Dame point guard Hannah Hidalgo and LSU’s Mikaylah Williams — the consensus group right behind Watkins — can also choose to return to their American colleges.

“It makes draft planning even tougher for teams and GMs,” said Rebecca Lobo, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer who called South Carolina-USC for ESPN. "If JuJu Watkins enters the draft, the impact would be immense both on and off the court for Toronto. She is the type of talent you build a franchise around. Not only an incredible player but she already has a big brand that will help drive ticket sales and viewers. JuJu could be a massive cornerstone for the Tempo.”
Watkins (12) has said she wants to win a NCAA title with her hometown USC before she turns pro. (Melina Pizano/Getty Images)

Where does Watkins stand? Well, the only thing she has offered publicly is that she won’t address her draft status until after USC’s season has concluded. Watkins is L.A.-born and she has repeatedly said her dream is to win a college title in her hometown.

Wright Rogers said on Sunday night that the Tempo front office is in constant communication with college coaches and agents and that will clearly be the case here. Watkins is represented by Klutch Sports Group, which is the agency that also represents NBA star LeBron James.

“Now that we have some direction, we really can hone in on understanding the plan that these athletes have for their future,” Wright Rogers said. “It’s going to be very complicated and it may come down to the wire. Each player has about 48 hours after their last NCAA game to declare. We will stay proactively locked in.”

blocks.text: The positives for Watkins to come out in 2027 are what you’d expect. She can compete against the best players in the world, the WNBA is a better launching pad for a shot at the U.S. Olympic team, and playing in Canada will give her the opportunity to market herself not just to a city but an entire country

But here is where it gets tricky. Watkins is a high-profile U.S. college athlete and already has significant Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) deals with companies such as Nike, Gatorade, and Fanatics. Her 2026 college earnings will almost unquestionably top what she would earn in salary in the WNBA next season. (The salary for the 2027 WNBA No. 1 pick could be as high as $565,000 for next year’s top pick under the new collective bargaining agreement.) Staying in college will continue to make her wealthy.

There is also this: Watkins and her management team might want to place her in a U.S. market. They could roll the dice that her hometown L.A. Sparks (who next season have their own pick as well as the Chicago Sky’s pick) crash out and land the No. 1 pick in the 2028 draft.
Madison Booker (35) is another top prospect the Tempo will be watching. (Christian Petersen/Getty Images)

The good news is the Tempo are likely to land an all-star calibre prospect even if Watkins declines to come out. Booker is a 6-foot-1 forward who can efficiently score from both mid-range and the perimeter — the kind of player that wins you championships. She can defend power forwards given her strength in the post. So far this season she is averaging 21 points per game on 57 per cent shooting. It is very unlikely she will return to Texas.

Hidalgo is one of the best point guard prospects in years, an insanely prolific scorer and a disruptive player on defence who broke the NCAA Division I single-season steals record last season with 202. Her only flaw is size – she’s just 5-foot-7. But so far bigger guards have been unable to stop her. She is averaging an obscene 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals this season. LSU’s Williams (a 6-foot guard with a very quick release) is probably next on the list. It is still a very deep draft if everyone opts to come out outside of Watkins.
“Throughout the history of this league, getting the number one pick does alter the trajectory of your franchise,” Wright Rogers said.

There was a significant fiscal commitment from Tempo ownership to be competitive in 2026 — Toronto made Marina Mabrey and Brittany Sykes the league’s first million-dollar backcourt — but things unraveled quickly. The team was ravaged by injuries, finishing at 11-33 including losing 22 of their last 24 games. How bad did it get? The Tempo ranked first overall in games lost to in-season injuries and the quartet of Sykes, Mabrey, Nyara Sabally, and Kiki Rice — the team’s most talented players— played a total of just 78 minutes together this season.

“We are putting in the work to ensure that we don't have the situation with injuries again,” Wright Rogers said. “We're putting in a lot of time reshaping our health and performance group, putting a microscope under the group, and putting resources and the backing into that space so we won't be repeating those same injury woes that we had last season.”

blocks.text: Toronto currently has six players under contract for 2027 (Mabrey, Sykes, Kiki Rice, Julie Allemand, Aneesah Morrow and Teonni Key) and more than $4 million available in cap space. The No. 1 pick gives them roster construction options and also offers the enticement for free agents to play with a potential franchise player.

Wright Rogers did not formally say that she would pick Watkins during a post-lottery call with reporters if Watkins declares for the pros, but the Tempo boss most certainly will call her name if the star comes out. Given all of this, here is the one bit of advice we can offer as we enter the beginning of JuJu Watch:
If you are a fan of the Toronto Tempo, you should root very hard for the USC Trojans to win the NCAA women’s basketball title next spring.
